plan.summary: One Inbox page with a repeatable ?assignee= filter (people plus Unassigned, defaulting to the reader, cleared with ?assignee=everyone), the Mine/Everyone switch, the Unassigned band and the inbox.view preference removed, every needs-you count scoped to the reader's own assigned unsnoozed human-turn asks plus credential requests, and the Agents card's second number counted from agent-turn rows in its own right. Client-side only: no change to GET /api/v1/inbox.
plan.surface: The Dispatch dashboard itself - real Go server, built SPA, real browser - driven by packages/dispatch/e2e (Playwright). The issue pod has no psql, docker, Postgres or root, so the recorded proof is the `dispatch` job of .github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml at the pull request head; the re-runnable command on a machine with a pgvector Postgres is in plan.md.

findings.finding: 1. An ask nobody is assigned reaches no inbox and no count anywhere, including an agent's approval request and every project-document ask; skills/dispatch/references/asks.md:10-11 and approval.e2e.ts:594-613 still say otherwise.
findings.answer: Accepted as the human's settled design (the spec's own closing section says a reader adds Unassigned to the filter to see them). The plan adds the task to rewrite skills/dispatch/references/asks.md:10-11 and approval.e2e.ts:594-613, and plan.md's 'What agents lose' section reports the consequence to the architect.

findings.finding: 2. A live 'Assign to me' write is unmounted by the filter that drops its row, which is exactly the Unassigned filter where the button is offered.
findings.answer: Decision 9 and step 5: the list keeps any row whose assign write is live, as inShutBand already keeps a row whose snooze write is live; a unit test with a failing useIssueAssignee under the Unassigned filter pins the refusal and Retry staying on screen.

findings.finding: 3. With the Unassigned band gone, another person's question lands under the heading 'Waiting on you'.
findings.answer: Decision 5 and step 2: the first band reads 'Waiting on you' only when the filter is the reader alone, and 'Waiting on a person' otherwise; InboxGroups takes the titles record as a prop. Recorded as a departure from the spec's 'the bands stay as they are'.

findings.finding: 4. The empty state has no wording per filter, and the spec's 'Nothing needs you' sentence is only true of a reader with no credential requests (Inbox.tsx:318-332, inbox-and-asks.md:38-41).
findings.answer: Step 5 fixes one string per case (reader alone, cleared, any other selection, agent unchanged) with a test each, and keeps the documented rule that none of them is said while a credential request is listed. No code change is read out of that spec sentence.

findings.finding: 5. ?section=needs-you was absent from the outline and would disagree with the Agents pill it serves.
findings.answer: Decision 8 and step 7: section=needs-you keeps meaning turn-and-not-snoozed, the reader's part comes from the default filter the pill's link leaves alone, and an e2e assertion holds the pill's number equal to the rows its link opens.

findings.finding: 6. The page's ?assignee= would carry the opposite default from the server's ?assignee= on /api/v1/inbox, and 'absent means me' makes a shared link show the recipient's own work.
findings.answer: Decision 2: the vocabulary is kept (emails, unassigned, everyone) with a comment at parseInboxSearch naming the server's opposite default, and picking yourself writes your own email into the address, so a link a reader sends shows what the sender saw.

findings.finding: 7. Unknown, unlisted and mixed-case emails in the address have no rule.
findings.answer: Decision 10 and step 1: values are trimmed and lowercased, an unknown one matches nothing and is refused by nobody (the split is client-side), and it stays selected in the filter so the reader can take it off. Covered by routes.test.ts and an Inbox test.

findings.finding: 8. buildInboxPath() call sites would silently reset the reader's filter.
findings.answer: Decision 8 and steps 5 and 7: the agent chip's clear keeps the assignee filter, BlockedOnYou keeps linking to the default list it counts, the 'Needs you' pill keeps the default filter and the 'Waiting on agent' pill links with the filter cleared. routes.test.ts and an e2e step cover it.

findings.finding: 9. The drawer loses the state channel the view switch used, and InboxDrawer.test.tsx:68-93 loses its subject.
findings.answer: Step 8: the drawer holds its own selection (absent to start, which is the reader) and passes it with a callback, so changing it writes nothing to the address and does not close the drawer; that is the replacement assertion.

findings.finding: 10. The project pill: omitting credential requests departs from the spec's sentence, and the pill links to a page showing a different number.
findings.answer: Decision 6, recorded as a spec departure for the architect: the pill applies the same rule to that project's rows and carries no credential request, since one belongs to no project. The link stays as it is and the mismatch is stated in plan.md.

findings.finding: 11. The second Agents number's predicate (snoozed rows in or out) and the fate of agent.open_asks were unstated.
findings.answer: Decision 7 and step 7: it counts the session's rows whose waiting_on is 'agent', snoozes ignored; agent.open_asks keeps its role in hasDispatchSignal and orderAgents; a test with a snoozed human-turn ask pins it in neither number.

findings.finding: 12. Escape inside the filter popover meets the Inbox's three Escape bindings and the drawer's.
findings.answer: Step 5: the page withholds its 'clear the selection' binding while the popover is open, so one press closes the popover and nothing else; covered by a unit test and a keyboard e2e assertion on the page and in the drawer.

findings.finding: 13. The marks rule is documented and tested in terms of Mine and Everyone (AGENTS.md:192, keyboard-inbox.e2e.ts:249-285, :527-561).
findings.answer: Steps 10 and 11: the rule is restated in filter terms (a mark whose row the filter excludes neither counts nor writes), the two keyboard e2e tests are rewritten as filter changes rather than deleted, and AGENTS.md:192 is updated.

findings.finding: 14. A shared usersQuery() enabled by default would make every issue page fetch /api/v1/users; and the filter has no stated pending or failed wording.
findings.answer: Step 3 keeps `enabled` at each call site (the badge lazy as today, the filter enabled when its popover first opens), and step 4 names the pending and failed strings, with the filter still working from the address when the list cannot load.

findings.finding: 15. The filter's trigger text, accessible name and the one selector tests use were unstated.
findings.answer: Step 4 fixes them: the trigger reads 'Assignee · you', '· everyone', '· Unassigned', '· <email>' or '· N', and its accessible name is 'Filter by assignee', which is the handle every rewritten test uses.

findings.finding: 16. Deleting inbox.view breaks userPreference.test.tsx, whose subject is the storage rule rather than the Inbox.
findings.answer: Step 9: that test is re-pointed at a surviving member rather than rewritten, and decision 3 records that stale dispatch.inbox.view:<login> entries are left in readers' browsers.

findings.finding: 17. The documentation list was short by four files, one of them agent-facing.
findings.answer: Step 11 names them all: skills/dispatch/references/asks.md:10-11, docs/site/.../agents.md:19-21, issues-and-projects.md:27-28, index.md:41-43, the extra passages inside inbox-and-asks.md (:30-32, :38-41) and AGENTS.md (:192, :254).

findings.finding: 18. The named verification command covered one spec on one browser, and the screenshot criterion is not machine-checkable.
findings.answer: The acceptance section names the full spec set (inbox, inbox-grouping, inbox-drawer, inbox-stability, keyboard-inbox, approval, issue, phone, workspace, agents, project) with no --project narrowing, and the screenshot line is marked a reviewer eye check; the docs build regenerates the picture from this same harness.

findings.finding: 19. The claim about this machine's tools was unverified.
findings.answer: Restated with its evidence in plan.md: `command -v psql` and `command -v docker` answer nothing in the issue pod, no Postgres server is installed and the account is not root, so the proof is CI's dispatch job and each phase re-checks its own pod for a reachable Postgres first.

findings.finding: 20. Snooze under somebody else's filter, and whether the banner appears under an agent filter, were unaddressed.
findings.answer: Decision 4 and step 5: a snooze is the reader's own, so Later holds what the reader deferred whoever the filter names; the banner stays hidden while the list is narrowed to one agent, as today, and reads the whole list rather than the filtered one.

specDepartures.spec: Every count of work waiting on the reader means one thing, whatever the filter is set to: open questions whose next move is a person's, on issues assigned to that reader, that the reader has not snoozed, plus the credential requests Dispatch already puts to them. That is ... the 'Blocked on you' pill on a project page.
specDepartures.plan: The project page's pill counts that project's open questions assigned to the reader and not snoozed, and no credential request; it keeps the shape it has today.
specDepartures.evidence: A credential request belongs to no project: packages/dispatch/web/src/features/credentials/pending.ts:29-35 is one global list, and ProjectPage.tsx:63-67 reads a project-scoped inbox of its own, which is why BlockedOnYou.tsx:68-69 already documents that the project pill carries none. Counting them there would make a project's number partly about another page.

specDepartures.spec: The bands within the list stay as they are: Waiting on you, then Waiting on agents, then Later for the questions the reader has snoozed.
specDepartures.plan: All three bands and their order stay. The first band's heading reads 'Waiting on you' only while the filter names the reader alone, and 'Waiting on a person' otherwise.
specDepartures.evidence: sections.ts:55 diverts every row that is not the reader's into the Unassigned band today, so no other person's question has ever appeared under 'Waiting on you'. With that band gone (sections.ts:50-57 falling through to row.waiting_on), a filter naming somebody else would head their questions with the reader's own second person, on the one screen whose banner counts only the reader's.
